transforms.description: An assistant message's content keeps only the text after its last </think>, with leading newlines removed; the reasoning before it is re-emitted inside <think> only for turns after the last user query, and dropped from earlier turns.
A past model turn's content drops every <|channel>...<channel|> thinking block (macro strip_thinking) and is then trimmed.
Message content, or each text part of it, is rendered through |trim, so leading and trailing whitespace is removed.
A leading system message is not rendered under its own role: its content, followed by a blank line, is prefixed to the first user turn.

A past assistant turn renders only its content, on the final channel; its thinking (the analysis channel) is dropped. A tool-call turn's analysis is kept only while no later assistant turn without tool calls follows.

Tool definitions render as a TypeScript namespace between "namespace functions {" and "} // namespace functions": each tool as "// <description>" then "type <name> = (_: {", each top-level parameter as a "// <description>" line when it has one, then "<name>: <type>" with "?" after the name when it is not required, then ", // default: <default>" when it has one (raw beside an enum, as JSON otherwise) and ","; the tool closes with "}) => any;". A tool without parameters, or with no properties, is "type <name> = () => any;". Types print as TypeScript: a string enum as its quoted values joined by " | ", an array as its element type plus [], a nested object as {<name>: <type>, ...} with "?" on names it does not require, an object without properties as object, and " | null" after a nullable string or array. Accepted for OpenAI-style tools (type function around a function holding only name, description and parameters) whose parameters are standard JSON Schema: every node typed string, number, integer, boolean, null, array or object, carrying nothing beyond a description, a non-empty string enum on a string, items on an array, properties and a required list naming only them on an object, a JSON default, and nullable true; the parameters object itself holds only type object, properties and required. Documented losses, which the port prints exactly as the template does: integer prints as number; the null type prints as any; a description or default below the top-level parameters is not printed; an array of string, number, integer or boolean items prints as the bare element type (string[], number[], boolean[]), so the items' description, enum and default are not printed; an element type longer than 50 characters prints as any[], so nothing inside the items is printed; a non-string default beside an enum is concatenated raw, so a number or boolean prints as JavaScript writes it, a list as its items joined by commas (none as undefined, a nested list or mapping as JSON), and a mapping as [object Map]. Refused, so the tool stays unexplained: any other schema keyword (oneOf, anyOf, $ref, format, additionalProperties and the rest), a type list, nullable on anything but a string without an enum or an array (the template does not print it there), nullable on scalar items, a none default beside an enum (the concatenation fails on it), a description or default on the parameters object (never read), nesting deeper than 16 levels (a bound on hostile input), and any other function key (no pinned template reads strict).

Each tool renders between <|tool> and <tool|> as declaration:<name>{description:<|"|><description><|"|>,parameters:{properties:{...},required:[...],type:<|"|>OBJECT<|"|>}}, the parameters part only when the tool has parameters, its properties and required parts only when non-empty. Properties go in case-insensitive key order at every level, each as <key>:{description,enum,items,nullable,properties,required,type} with its description only when non-empty, its enum only on a string, its items (key by key in case-insensitive order: properties as above, required as a list, type upper-cased, anything else through format_argument) only on an array, nullable:true when set, its properties and a non-empty required list only on an object, and its type upper-cased; every string sits between <|"|> tokens. A function's response follows the parameters as ,response:{description:<|"|>...<|"|>,type:<|"|>OBJECT<|"|>}. Accepted for OpenAI-style tools (type function around a function holding only name, description, parameters and response) whose parameters are standard JSON Schema: every node typed string, number, integer, boolean, null, array or object, carrying nothing beyond a description, a non-empty string enum on a string, items on an array, properties and a required list naming only them on an object, a JSON default, and nullable true; the parameters object itself holds only type object, properties and required; the response holds a string type and, optionally, a string description. Documented losses, which the port prints exactly as the template does: a property's own default is not printed (an item's is); a response type is printed only when it upper-cases to OBJECT, and otherwise the response's brace is never closed. One pinned variant prints the response differently, and a site holding its text passes too: lmstudio-community/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-QAT-MLX-4bit@aa5e2e50376f54254d503276ca2222ea8569b95e:chat_template.jinja lines 1-13 and 122-136 print any non-empty response type upper-cased, put a comma only between the description and the type, and always close the brace. Refused, so the tool stays unexplained: any other schema keyword, a type list, an enum that is not a non-empty list of strings on a string, nullable other than true, a property named description, type, properties, required or nullable (some pinned variants skip it), none anywhere inside a printed default (the variants differ), a default on an object without properties (the template would print it as a property), a description or default on the parameters object (never read), a response holding any other key or a type that is not a string (its |upper fails), nesting deeper than 16 levels (a bound on hostile input), and any other function key.

Each tool renders between <start_function_declaration> and <end_function_declaration> as the gemma-4 declaration does, with strings between <escape> tokens, every property's description printed (empty when it has none), no nullable on a property and no response. Accepted for OpenAI-style tools (type function around a function holding only name, description and parameters) whose parameters are standard JSON Schema: every node typed string, number, integer, boolean, null, array or object, carrying nothing beyond a description, a non-empty string enum on a string, items on an array, properties and a required list naming only them on an object, and a JSON default, with nullable true allowed on array items (printed there through format_argument); the parameters object itself holds only type object, properties and required. Documented loss, which the port prints exactly as the template does: a property's own default is not printed (an item's is). Refused, so the tool stays unexplained: any other schema keyword, a type list, an enum that is not a non-empty list of strings on a string, nullable on a property (the template never reads it), a property named description, type, properties, required or nullable (the template skips it), none anywhere inside a printed default, a default on an object without properties, a description or default on the parameters object (never read), nesting deeper than 16 levels (a bound on hostile input), and any other function key.

Tool definitions render as an XML list between <tools> and </tools>: each tool as <function> with its <name>, its trimmed <description> and <parameters>; each parameter as <parameter> with its <name>, its <type> when it has one, its trimmed <description> when it has one, its enum as <enum>[`a`, 1, true]</enum>, then every other key in its own order as a tag holding its JSON (a mapping) or its string form (anything else, a list as JSON), then its own required list; then the tool's required list as <required>[`x`, `y`]</required> when non-empty, then </parameters>, then the function's return as <return>...</return> when it has one (JSON for a mapping, its string form otherwise), and </function>. The template prints every key a parameter holds, so any JSON shape there is accepted: type lists, oneOf, $ref, format, nullable, additionalProperties and the rest. Accepted for tools, OpenAI-style or a bare function, holding only name, description, parameters and return, whose parameters object holds type object (never printed, so held to object), properties and, optionally, a required list. Documented losses, which the port prints exactly as the template does: descriptions are trimmed; a key's tag is normalised (- and space become _, $ is dropped), so keys that differ only there print alike; a value printed in its string form shows a string and the number or boolean it spells alike ("1" and 1, "true" and true); an empty required list prints as nothing, as no list does. Refused, so the tool stays unexplained: none where the template prints a value in its string form (|string fails on it), a description that is not a string (|trim fails), an empty enum (it would print as nothing, as no enum does, though it means the opposite), an enum or required list holding anything but strings, numbers and booleans, a value that is not JSON or nests deeper than 16 levels (a bound on hostile input), anything else on the parameters object (never read), and any other function key. A tool without parameters stops the template, so it is never explained.
